chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Balad from Sa'd al-Iskaf who said:af who said: I know him to have said from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him):

Among the Children of Israel there was a worshipper, so Dawud (peace be upon him) liked him for it. Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to him saying: 'Let not anything in his matter please you, for he is a show-off.'
He said: The man died, and Dawud (peace be upon him) was informed, and it was said to him: 'The man has died.' Dawud (peace be upon him) said: 'Bury your companion.'
He said: The Children of Israel disapproved and said: 'Why did he not attend (the funeral)?'
He said: When he was washed (for burial), fifty men stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good.
He said: When they performed the funeral prayer for him, fifty others stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good.
When they buried him, fifty (more) stood up and testified by Allah that they knew of him only good.
Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'What prevented you from testifying (attending the funeral) for so-and-so?'
Dawud (peace be upon him) said: 'O my Lord, because of what You revealed to me regarding his matter.'

He said: Allah, the Mighty, the Glorious, sent revelation to him saying: 'That is so, but a people of learned men and monks have testified that they knew of him only good, so I accepted their testimony regarding him and forgave (overlooked) My knowledge of him.'

This is the end of the Book of Testimonimonies from al-Kafi, composed by Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, may Allah have mercy on him, and it is followed by the Book of Judgments and Rulings, if Allah the Exalted wills.

key_terms.أَحْبَار: Learned men; scholars of the Torah.
key_terms.صَلَّوْا عَلَيْهِ: Performed the funeral prayer for him.
key_terms.غَفَرْتُ لَهُ عِلْمِي: I forgave/overlooked My knowledge (of his true state).
key_terms.غُسِّلَ: Washed (ritual bathing of the deceased for burial).
key_terms.مُرَاءٍ: Show-off; performing acts of worship for the sake of being seen by others.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between divine knowledge and human testimony regarding a person's piety in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narrative from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) by contrasting Prophet Dawud’s divine insight into the worshipper’s hidden *mura'ah* (show-off) with the limited perspective of the masses. It illustrates that while human testimony is accepted for general burial rites, ultimate forgiveness rests on Allah’s complete knowledge of the heart, a key concept in Shia eschatology regarding the balance between outward actions and inner intent.
